strengths: Well-motivated practical problem: addresses real limitations of existing feed-forward methods (fixed input views) and per-scene optimization (computational cost), with clear applications to robotics and real-time systems

Comprehensive system design integrating multiple well-justified components: 3D-annotation-free training framework, novel view selection based on coverage masks, instance-guided contrastive learning with O(NpK) complexity vs O(N²p), and geometry-semantic hierarchical sparsification recognizing differing spatial density requirements

Strong experimental validation showing consistent improvements across sparse to dense views (2-32) with stable performance, ~200× speedup over per-scene optimization (5sec vs 10+ min), and better semantic accuracy than optimization-based baselines
Valuable InstanceMV-14K dataset contribution with 15M+ images and instance masks from diverse sources, addressing the lack of large-scale multi-view semantic data
Practical efficiency focus demonstrated by meaningful memory/computation reductions (2.6M vs 6.4M embeddings) through geometry-semantic sparsification while maintaining quality
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: directly inherits VGGT architecture, uses standard projection-based novel view selection, applies prior voxel-based sparsification [10,17], and makes straightforward adaptations of contrastive learning; contribution is primarily in system engineering rather than algorithmic innovation

Heavy VGGT dependency creates circular reasoning: quality bounded by VGGT, and '3D-annotation-free' claim is misleading as it shifts annotation to VGGT's training; no ablation comparing VGGT pseudo-labels versus alternative supervision or quantifying data contribution vs method improvement

Narrow evaluation scope: restricted to indoor scenes (ScanNet/ScanNet++) with no outdoor or diverse environment testing; semantic evaluation limited to pre-annotated mIoU/mAcc metrics without evaluating truly open-vocabulary queries; promised robotic navigation/manipulation applications not validated; 3D editing shown only qualitatively

Insufficient technical justification for key design choices: 3D feature aggregation via voxel-based CLIP averaging (Eq. 5-6) lacks justification; covariance fusion via moment-matching + isotropic approximation (Eq. 11-12) has no comparison to alternatives; coverage threshold τ sensitivity and MLP architecture in Eq. 5 not discussed; instance mask sampling strategy (Eq. 6) lacks clarity

Evaluation setup concerns: baselines designed for 2-view inputs; extending to multi-view via DUSt3R may not be entirely fair; dense-view comparison (Table 2) uses 16/32 views inconsistently with feed-forward comparisons spanning 2-32 views; ablations (Table 3) only on ScanNet++, missing ScanNet validation

Dataset construction transparency issues: SAM2 used for unlabeled data masks without quality analysis or impact assessment; reproduction instructions for InstanceMV-14K not clearly specified; unclear how to obtain RealEstate10K subset used

Incomplete ablations: missing studies on coverage threshold τ sensitivity, FLEG performance with/without InstanceMV-14K dataset, semantic Gaussian count necessity analysis, and failure mode characterization

Reproducibility concerns: many hyperparameters (voxel sizes εgeo/εsem, coverage threshold τ, MLP architecture) incompletely specified; no code or dataset release mentioned; training details for InstanceMV-14K construction lacking

Generalization and scalability: limited evidence for cross-dataset generalization; 1B parameter model raises scalability questions; no evaluation on challenging scenarios (extreme poses, specular surfaces, outdoor scenes); semantic embedding consistency across views not analyzed
Presentation gaps: Figure 2 overly complex; geometry-semantic density trade-off in sparsification not explicitly discussed; no user studies validating semantic query quality

strengths: Addresses practical problem of arbitrary-view feed-forward reconstruction with demonstrated stability across 2-32 views; existing methods degrade significantly with more views but FLEG maintains ~47% mIoU
Strong experimental validation with comprehensive comparisons (8 baselines), multiple metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, mIoU, mAcc), and two datasets showing consistent improvements
Significant efficiency advantage over per-scene optimization: 1.89-3.20s inference vs. 10-20+ minutes, enabling real-time applications

Thoughtful system design including: (1) coverage-based novel view selection grounded in visibility, (2) instance-guided contrastive learning reducing computational complexity from O(N²_p) to O(N_p K), and (3) geometry-semantic hierarchical sparsification recognizing different spatial density requirements
InstanceMV-14K dataset contribution with 15M+ images and instance masks, enabling 3D-annotation-free training
Sound technical execution and honest ablation studies demonstrating component importance
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: network architecture, camera/depth heads directly from VGGT [30]; training is standard distillation with pseudo-labels; instance-guided contrastive learning is straightforward application of known techniques; sparsification uses standard voxelization. Reads as effective engineering rather than fundamental innovation.

Critical dependency on external models obscures true contribution: VGGT provides initialization, geometric supervision, and camera parameters; CLIP provides semantic features; SAM2 provides instance annotations. Unclear how much performance comes from proposed method vs. these pre-trained models. No ablation removing VGGT initialization.

Unfair baseline comparisons: LSM and Uni3R designed for fixed views are adapted via DUSt3R post-processing (mentioned casually), making comparison questionable. Only 2 per-scene baselines for dense views. Recent feed-forward methods (AnySplat, IGGT) not compared quantitatively.

Narrow evaluation domain limits generalization claims: only indoor scenes (ScanNet/ScanNet++), unknown performance on outdoor/diverse scenes. Semantic ground truth may be inconsistent with CLIP's class definitions, affecting metric reliability.

Missing critical analysis: no failure cases discussed, no sensitivity analysis on key hyperparameters (coverage threshold τ, voxel sizes ϵ_geo/ϵ_sem), no investigation of when isotropic approximation works, training computational costs not reported

Reproducibility concerns: InstanceMV-14K uses internet video data with potential licensing issues; code release not mentioned; voxel size values not specified; 3D feature aggregation not formally defined early in paper; circular dependency on VGGT makes reproduction difficult

Semantic embedding remains fundamentally model-dependent despite 'annotation-free' claims: relies on CLIP (limiting sub-object semantic understanding), SAM2 (external model), and instance-level learning cannot capture fine-grained semantics

Incomplete ablations: Table 3 doesn't isolate VGGT initialization contribution (likely substantial), view selection threshold τ, or compare against simpler baselines (e.g., direct semantic head fine-tuning)

Presentation issues: dense with many components making key novel contributions hard to isolate; sections 3.3-3.4 have conceptual overlap; some design choices lack justification (why isotropic Gaussians specifically for semantics?)

Novel 3D-annotation-free training framework that cleverly leverages VGGT geometric supervision and large-scale 2D video data with instance masks, avoiding expensive 3D annotations
Flexibility across variable view counts (2-32+ views) in a single model, unlike prior feed-forward methods constrained to fixed input views
Well-motivated technical contributions: instance-guided contrastive learning (O(N_p·K) vs O(N_p²) complexity), geometry-semantic hierarchical sparsification exploiting semantic sparsity
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple view settings with consistent outperformance on both reconstruction quality (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) and semantic accuracy (mIoU/mAcc)

Clear paper presentation with well-motivated design choices and effective visualizations of results

Overstated 'annotation-free' claim: method heavily depends on VGGT pseudo-labels for geometric supervision; no analysis of sensitivity to VGGT errors or failure modes

Semantic evaluation limited to open-vocabulary query metrics; missing analysis of cross-view consistency, fine-grained categories, and failure cases (occlusions, rare objects)
Incomplete design analysis: voxel sizes (ϵ_geo, ϵ_sem) lack sensitivity analysis, isotropic Gaussian approximation (Eq. 12) not theoretically justified, sparsification trade-offs not quantified
InstanceMV-14K construction underspecified: filtering criteria, SAM2 failure rate, quality control, and data biases not discussed; dataset availability unclear
Reconstruction quality at sparse views (2 views: PSNR 24.20, SSIM 0.776) is moderate; unclear reliability at extreme sparse scenarios

Missing critical details: training time/memory requirements not reported, hyperparameter sensitivity not explored, no failure case analysis or discussion of fundamental limitations of feed-forward approaches
No explicit failure analysis or discussion of when optimization-based methods remain necessary despite feed-forward speed advantage

strengths: Well-motivated problem addressing practical limitations of prior feed-forward methods (fixed views, pose requirements); supports flexible 2-32+ input views without pose.
Key insight on semantic sparsity: DGLE module achieves 95% storage reduction (18.04 MB vs 491.3 MB) while maintaining comparable semantic fidelity, with clear validation in Appendix C.
Technically sound dual-branch distillation framework with novel-view-based supervision to prevent overfitting; instance-guided contrastive learning is computationally efficient (O(N_p K) vs O(N_p²)).

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: multiple views (2-32), datasets (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica), metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, mIoU, mAcc); consistent improvements over baselines (mIoU 46.61 vs 39.54 at 2 views).
Training without 3D annotations or semantic labels; uses readily-available 2D instance masks from SAM2; enables scalable training on video sequences.
Multi-task capabilities (novel-view synthesis, open-vocabulary query, 3D editing) in single model with clear qualitative improvements (Figs. 3-4).
Well-written, clearly structured paper with thorough ablation studies (Table 3) validating each component and cross-dataset generalization on Replica.
weaknesses: Strictly limited to indoor scenes (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica); no outdoor evaluation undermines generalization claims and severely limits real-world applicability.
Performance ceiling bounded by VGGT; Table 4 shows FLEG achieves only 0.681 AUC@15 vs VGGT's 0.668 at 32 views—geometric accuracy cannot exceed distillation source, a fundamental limitation.

Limited component novelty: individual techniques are standard (VGGT distillation from prior work, CLIP features, instance contrastive learning); primary contribution is DGLE module and novel-view selection, which are incremental.

Questionable experimental setup: LSM and Uni3R evaluated using two-view pretrained models selecting nearest views to target, handicapping methods not designed for sparse multi-view settings; subset evaluation for 32-view optimization baselines (Table 2).
Semantic sparsity assumption appears data-dependent; v_sem=0.016 choice is empirically tuned (Appendix C); unclear how the 5% storage claim generalizes to other domains or semantic distributions.
Many hyperparameters (η₁, η₂, λ₁₋₄, τ, voxel sizes) with no sensitivity analysis or cross-validation methodology described; robustness unclear.
GPU memory constraints unresolved—while storage reduced, handling hundreds/thousands of views still limited; no runtime comparisons with baselines provided.
Incomplete semantic evaluation: mIoU/mAcc only evaluate segmentation, not semantic quality; no perceptual evaluation, user studies, or analysis of failure modes on complex multi-semantic scenes.

Missing analysis: no discussion of failure cases, when semantic sparsity breaks down, or why FLEG outperforms baselines beyond sparsity; isotropic Gaussian approximation (Eq. 11) justified mainly by convenience.
Technical clarity issues: MLP architecture for L_feat (Eq. 5) unspecified; 3D feature aggregation module mentioned but not formally defined; notation Π in Eq. 1 could be clearer.

strengths: Comprehensive experimental validation across multiple datasets (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica) with both reconstruction and semantic metrics, including extensive ablations
Strong and consistent empirical results, particularly on semantic metrics (46.87% mIoU vs 39.54% baseline at 2 views), with good generalization to unseen dataset
DGLE module demonstrates practical utility by achieving comparable semantic fidelity with only ~5% of per-Gaussian embeddings, reducing storage overhead
Well-motivated problem addressing real limitations of prior feed-forward methods (fixed view counts, camera parameter requirements)
Clear presentation with good visualizations and systematic methodology description
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: VGGT distillation and baseline novel-view selection are borrowed techniques; instance-guided contrastive learning is a minor variation; DGLE is parameter aggregation rather than a novel representation

Heavy dependence on foundation models (VGGT, CLIP, SAM2) creates a bounded ceiling on performance; unclear what FLEG contributes beyond integration of existing methods; geometric accuracy limited by VGGT (Tables 4-5)
Baseline comparison fairness issues: LSM and Uni3R tested only with 2-view pretrained models despite evaluation at 4-16 views; dense-view comparison (Table 2) limited to subset of scenes
Limited spatial scope to indoor scenes (ScanNet++, ScanNet, Replica) undermines claims of 'any views' and applicability to robotics; acknowledged in Appendix I but unaddressed

Overclaimed contributions: 'semantic sparsity' is intuitive for categorical semantics; Table 3 lines 2-3 show denser variants achieve slightly better mIoU, contradicting sparsity narrative; 'compact semantic representation' is parameter reduction, not methodological advance

Missing critical ablations and analyses: coverage threshold τ (Eq. 2) selection not discussed; MLP in Eq. 5 purpose unexplained; no runtime/memory analysis; no failure case discussion; semantic metric improvements not decomposed between geometric vs. semantic contributions
Semantic distillation still requires 2D instance masks from SAM2, contradicting the claim of training 'without semantic labels'; dependency on external foundation models not adequately justified

Incomplete baseline fairness and technical clarity: voxel size selection criteria absent; isotropic semantic Gaussian approximation (Eq. 11) not justified; moment-matching (Eq. 10) is standard technique; camera pose improvements modest (~1% in Table 4)

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem addressing real limitations of existing feed-forward language-embedded Gaussian methods (fixed view counts, semantic redundancy)
Novel insight that semantic representations are significantly sparser than geometric ones, with effective DGLE module achieving 20× storage reduction while maintaining performance

Technically sound dual-branch distillation framework with clever novel-view-based supervision avoiding complex self-supervised training, and instance-guided contrastive learning reducing complexity from O(N²_p) to O(N_p K)
Comprehensive and thorough experimental validation: consistent improvements across 2-32 views, cross-dataset generalization on Replica, detailed ablation studies, additional pose/depth comparisons
Strong empirical results with substantial improvements in semantic metrics (mIoU +5-8% over baselines) and reconstruction quality across PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS
Practical applicability: works without camera parameters or 3D annotations, enables training on arbitrary video data, clear path to real-time applications
Excellent presentation with clear motivation, effective figures, comprehensive supplementary material, and sufficient reproducibility details
weaknesses: Technical novelty is limited and largely incremental: dual-branch distillation applies standard knowledge distillation, novel-view selection uses coverage-based heuristics, and instance-guided contrastive learning employs relatively standard techniques

Evaluation scope restricted to indoor scenes (ScanNet, Replica); despite claims of arbitrary views, no outdoor evaluation provided. Cross-dataset generalization is mainly demonstrated on similar indoor domains
Geometric accuracy limited by VGGT as acknowledged (Section I), raising questions about the independence and fundamental contribution of the proposed approach
